article.title: BRICS Nations Join Hands to strengthen TCIM, Expert Working Group Taking Shape - PIB
article.summary: BRICS Nations Join Hands to strengthen TCIM, Expert Working Group Taking Shape PIB
article.full_text: India successfully hosted the BRICS Meeting on Traditional, Complementary and Integrative Medicine (TCIM) on 21 July 2026 at Chandigarh, as part of its BRICS 2026 Chairship. The meeting formed part of the broader four-day programme of BRICS Health Track events in Chandigarh, jointly organised by the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the Ministry of Ayush. The TCIM meeting brought together senior government officials, technical experts and delegates from BRICS member countries to strengthen multilateral cooperation, promote the exchange of knowledge and best practices, and advance collaboration in the field of Traditional, Complementary and Integrative Medicine. Held under the overarching BRICS Chairship theme, "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation & Sustainability," the meeting advanced collaboration among BRICS nations to promote evidence-based traditional medicine systems, strengthen institutional partnerships and contribute towards sustainable and resilient healthcare systems. The meeting witnessed participation from the BRICS member states—Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Iran, Russia, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates—providing a platform to exchange best practices, policy experiences and scientific advancements in Traditional, Complementary and Integrative Medicine. The formal proceedings on TCIM commenced with a welcome address by Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, followed by opening remarks from member delegations. The Terms of Reference (ToR) for the proposed BRICS Expert Working Group on TCIM were finalised with the consensus of all available member states. The meeting also featured interactive discussions on strengthening collaboration, harmonising policy approaches and identifying future areas of cooperation among BRICS nations. A dedicated side event on "Capacity Building, Education and Human Resource Development" was also organised by the Ministry of Ayush. The session focused on strengthening global education and training in traditional medicine through academic collaborations, Ayush scholarship initiatives, faculty and student exchanges, research partnerships and evidence-generation mechanisms aimed at building a globally connected TCIM ecosystem. As part of India's BRICS Chairship 2026, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, also inaugurated the Ayush Zone, showcasing India's holistic healthcare initiatives. The Ayush Zone offered BRICS delegates an immersive experience of Ayush through Ayush Aahar, health and wellness consultations, India's herbal heritage, the Ministry's vision and global initiatives, and a dedicated hub on research, innovation and knowledge. Featuring wellness activities and Yoga, the Ayush Zone reflected India's commitment to fostering international collaboration in Traditional, Complementary and Integrative Medicine. The TCIM deliberations contributed to the broader BRICS Health Track led by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and supported ongoing discussions on strengthening healthcare cooperation among BRICS countries. The four-day programme also features a range of wellness and cultural activities showcasing India's holistic healthcare traditions. Delegates participated in Chair Yoga sessions, and will engage in Common Yoga Protocol (CYP) demonstrations organised by the Morarji Desai National Institute of Yoga (MDNIY), Yoga Break (Y-Break) sessions during meetings, and the Fit India Run. The Ayush Zone, along with the Ayush Aahar Mela curated with technical support from the National Institute of Ayurveda (NIA), showcased India's traditional healthcare ecosystem through health and wellness consultations, research and innovation exhibits, live Yoga demonstrations and other wellness activities, providing delegates with a comprehensive experience of the country's holistic healthcare traditions. The meeting delivered several significant outcomes, including progress towards the establishment of a BRICS Expert Working Group on Traditional, Complementary and Integrative Medicine; enhanced cooperation in research, education and regulatory frameworks; improved knowledge-sharing among member countries; and stronger recognition of Traditional, Complementary and Integrative Medicine within the BRICS Health agenda. The BRICS TCIM Meeting reflected India's continued commitment to promoting evidence-based traditional medicine, fostering international partnerships and advancing holistic, accessible and sustainable healthcare for all. story.title: The Folder That Became a Beginning
story.skipLabel: BRICS nations strengthen traditional medicine cooperation as an expert working group takes shape

creativeDirection.genre: warm workplace drama with light comedy
creativeDirection.dramaticPremise: At Chandigarh’s Ayush Zone, two delegates clash over leaving for a wellness activity when the finalisation of the BRICS Expert Working Group’s Terms of Reference turns one unfinished folder into a reason to stay and collaborate.

dramaticSpine.characterGoal: Leela wants Ravi to stay and shape their next collaboration around education and research.
dramaticSpine.obstacle: Ravi wants to leave the Ayush Zone before the next wellness activity and dismisses their unfinished notes as useless.
dramaticSpine.newsCatalyst: The BRICS member states reached consensus on the Terms of Reference for the proposed Expert Working Group on Traditional, Complementary and Integrative Medicine.
dramaticSpine.reversal: Ravi realises the folder is no longer a draft for a meeting; it can become preparation for future cooperation in research, education and knowledge-sharing.
dramaticSpine.costOfFailure: They may lose their chance to turn their shared idea into a practical collaboration before the programme moves on.
dramaticSpine.emotionalTurn: Ravi’s impatience gives way to cautious excitement.
dramaticSpine.resolution: Ravi gives up the immediate break and joins Leela at the research and education hub, carrying the folder forward.

visualBible.setting: A colourful animated Ayush Zone inside the BRICS Health Track programme in Chandigarh, with a nearby Ayush Aahar Mela counter, wellness consultation nook, research-and-innovation displays, and an open space for Yoga activities.
visualBible.colorAndLighting: Warm saffron, jade, turquoise and cream; bright Chandigarh afternoon light softened by the pavilion canopy, with gentle golden highlights on herbs and paper.
recurringProps: a blue cloth folder filled with handwritten collaboration notes
a small reusable cup of herbal drink
a sprig of fresh green herbs
visualBible.storyArc: The scene begins amid busy international wellness activity, tightens as Ravi tries to leave, reverses when the consensus on the expert group gives their notes new purpose, and ends with both characters moving toward the research and education hub together.
visualBible.referenceImagePrompt: Editorial animated-film still of two fictional BRICS delegates together in the Chandigarh Ayush Zone: Leela, an Indian woman in her early thirties wearing a mustard kurta and teal scarf; Ravi, a Brazilian man in his early thirties wearing a rust overshirt and cream trousers. They stand beside an Ayush Aahar Mela counter with a blue cloth folder, herbal drink cup, canvas shoulder bag and fresh herbs visible; research displays and an open Yoga area behind them, warm saffron-and-jade palette, afternoon canopy light, cinematic depth, caption-safe upper-third space, no text, logos, or watermark.

cast.voiceProfile: Warm, quick Indian-English voice with bright curiosity; starts focused and mildly exasperated, uses clipped pauses during the argument, then softens into delighted determination by the ending.
cast.visualIdentity: Indian woman in her early thirties, mustard kurta, teal scarf, practical sandals, blue cloth folder held close.

cast.voiceProfile: Low, playful Brazilian-English voice with relaxed pacing and dry comic timing; begins breezy and resistant, shifts into startled sincerity, ending with energetic commitment.
cast.visualIdentity: Brazilian man in his early thirties, rust overshirt, cream trousers, canvas shoulder bag, herbal drink cup in hand.

beats.dramaticAction: Ravi backs toward the pavilion exit while Leela blocks his path with the blue folder.
beats.turningPoint: His escape pauses when Leela reveals that the BRICS TCIM meeting has just created a new reason to keep their notes alive.

visual.caption: BRICS TCIM meeting advances cooperation
visual.imagePrompt: Editorial animated-film image of Leela stepping in front of Ravi at the Chandigarh Ayush Zone exit, blue cloth folder raised between them, Ayush Aahar counter and herbs behind, medium two-shot, warm afternoon canopy light, playful tension, recurring mustard kurta, teal scarf, rust overshirt, cream trousers, herbal cup and canvas bag, caption-safe upper-third space, no text, logos, or watermark
visual.scenePrompt: Continuous opening shot inside the animated Ayush Zone as Ravi tries to leave and Leela intercepts him.
visual.continuityNotes: Establish both characters and all recurring props; Ravi remains angled toward the exit, Leela holds the folder.

lines.speaker: Leela
lines.text: The BRICS TCIM meeting just finalised the Expert Working Group’s Terms of Reference.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: You blocked the exit for paperwork?

beats.dramaticAction: Ravi slips sideways; Leela catches the folder before it falls into the herbal drink counter.
beats.turningPoint: The near-spill forces Ravi to handle the folder, putting their unfinished collaboration directly in his hands.

visual.caption: One folder, suddenly important
visual.imagePrompt: Animated-film close action shot as Ravi lunges to catch Leela’s blue folder inches above a herbal drink counter, cup wobbling, fresh herbs and Ayush Zone activity behind, low-angle camera, bright jade and saffron lighting, comic nervous mood, recurring wardrobe and props, caption-safe upper-third space, no text, logos, or watermark
visual.scenePrompt: The same continuous scene tightens around the falling folder and wobbling cup.
visual.continuityNotes: Folder moves from Leela’s chest to Ravi’s hands; cup stays upright; exit remains behind Ravi.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: Careful! My drink nearly became international policy.

lines.speaker: Leela
lines.text: Hold it. We came for research and education partnerships, remember?

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: I came for five quiet minutes.

beats.dramaticAction: Leela pulls Ravi away from the counter and opens the folder as delegates pass toward the research hub.
beats.turningPoint: She connects the finalised framework to the wider exchange of knowledge and best practices, making departure feel like abandoning a live possibility.

visual.caption: Members agree on a proposed expert group
visual.imagePrompt: Animated editorial scene of Leela guiding Ravi toward a research-and-innovation hub while he carries the blue folder, passing delegates, herbal displays and a distant Yoga area, over-the-shoulder tracking camera, warm gold and turquoise light, purposeful mood, recurring wardrobe, cup, canvas bag and herbs, caption-safe upper-third space, no text, logos, or watermark
visual.scenePrompt: The camera tracks their movement from the food counter toward the research and education area.
visual.continuityNotes: Ravi now carries the folder; Leela walks beside him; the cup remains in his free hand.

lines.speaker: Leela
lines.text: All available members agreed. Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Iran, Russia, South Africa and the UAE.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: So our scribbles are not the plan.

lines.speaker: Leela
lines.text: No. They can become our next question.

beats.dramaticAction: A Yoga invitation draws Ravi toward the open activity space, but he stops and turns back to the research hub.
beats.turningPoint: Ravi gives up his immediate break, choosing to carry the folder into the future-facing discussion instead.

visual.caption: The break can wait
visual.imagePrompt: Animated-film wide shot of Ravi half-turning toward a welcoming Yoga activity while Leela gestures toward the research hub, blue folder tucked under his arm, herbal cup balanced carefully, busy Ayush Zone, soft afternoon light, comic hesitation turning sincere, recurring wardrobe and props, caption-safe upper-third space, no text, logos, or watermark
visual.scenePrompt: The continuous tracking shot reaches the fork between the Yoga area and the research hub.
visual.continuityNotes: The folder stays under Ravi’s arm; Leela’s teal scarf moves with her turn; both destinations remain visible.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: Chair Yoga is calling me. My spine has excellent timing.

lines.speaker: Leela
lines.text: Then carry it there. The discussions also covered policy, research and education.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: Fine. Five minutes became a working group.

beats.dramaticAction: Ravi hands Leela the folder, then turns and walks beside her into the research-and-innovation hub.
beats.turningPoint: Their immediate choice becomes a shared commitment to keep the collaboration moving, while the Yoga activity continues behind them.

visual.caption: Cooperation moves forward
visual.imagePrompt: Animated editorial-film closing shot of Ravi handing the blue folder back to Leela as they walk together into the Ayush research-and-innovation hub, Yoga activity glowing behind them, herbal cup and canvas bag visible, rear three-quarter camera, golden late-afternoon light, warm hopeful mood, recurring wardrobe and herbs, caption-safe upper-third space, no text, logos, or watermark
visual.scenePrompt: The same continuous scene ends with both delegates crossing into the hub together.
visual.continuityNotes: Leela receives the folder; Ravi keeps the cup and shoulder bag; the pavilion activity remains softly visible behind them.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: All right. You lead. I’ll bring the evidence—and the drink.

lines.speaker: Leela
lines.text: Deal. The framework is agreed; now we do the careful work.

story.exit: The two delegates disappear into the research-and-innovation hub together, leaving the Yoga activity and Ayush Aahar Mela alive behind them.
